summary.en: Use the **zero conditional** for facts and habits: _If you heat ice, it melts._ Use the **first conditional** for real possibilities in the future: _If it rains, we'll stay in._ After _if_, _when_, _as soon as_, _before_, _unless_ and _until_, use the **present** for the future, never _will_.
summary.es: En castellano usamos futuro o subjuntivo («si llueve, nos quedaremos»), pero en inglés tras if, when, as soon as o unless va presente: If it rains, we'll stay in. Will va solo en la otra parte de la frase.

form: Zero: **if / when** + present simple, present simple
First: **if** + present simple, **will / won't** + infinitive (or an imperative, or _can_, _may_, _should_)
Time clauses: **when / as soon as / until / before / after** + present simple (not _will_)
**unless** = _if … not_: _Unless you hurry, you'll be late._

uses.text: **General truths**: _If you mix blue and yellow, you get green._
**Habits and routines**: _If I miss the bus, I walk to work._
**Real future possibility**: _If you **ask** her, she'**ll** probably **help**._
**Future time clauses**: _I'll call you **as soon as** I **arrive**._ _Wait here **until** I **come** back._
**Instructions and offers**: _If you feel dizzy, sit down._ _If you need a lift, I can take you._
**Unless**: _We'll go for a walk **unless** it **snows**._ (Not _unless it doesn't_.)

note.en: Compare the second conditional for unlikely situations: If I won, I would buy a house. See the lesson on second and third conditionals.
note.es: Para situaciones poco probables o irreales, mira el segundo condicional.

mistakes.wrong: If it will rain tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.
mistakes.right: If it rains tomorrow, we'll cancel the picnic.

why.en: Do not use will after if. Use the present simple.
why.es: Tras if, presente: «si llueve» es if it rains.

mistakes.wrong: I'll phone you when I will get home.
mistakes.right: I'll phone you when I get home.

why.en: Time clauses with when also take the present simple for the future.
why.es: Con when, as soon as, etc., tampoco va will.

mistakes.wrong: Unless you don't hurry, you'll miss the train.
mistakes.right: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train.

why.en: Unless already means if … not, so the verb stays positive.
why.es: Unless ya lleva la negación: no uses not.

mistakes.wrong: If you will help me, I will finish sooner.
mistakes.right: If you help me, I'll finish sooner.

why.en: Will after if is only possible in polite requests (If you will wait here…), not in ordinary conditionals.
why.es: No pongas will tras if en condicionales normales.

examples.en: If you leave milk out in the sun, it goes off.
When the alarm rings, everyone has to leave the building.
examples.es: Cuando suena la alarma, todos tienen que salir del edificio.

examples.en: If I get the day off, I'll come and see you.
If you don't book soon, you won't find a cheap flight.
examples.es: Si no reservas pronto, no encontrarás un vuelo barato.

examples.en: I'll send you the photos as soon as I've uploaded them.
Don't open the door unless you know who it is.
If the printer jams again, call the technician.
We'll start the meeting when everybody has arrived.
If it's sunny on Sunday, we might have lunch in the garden.

practice.prompt: If I ___ the job, I'll move to Leeds.

explanation.en: First conditional: present simple after if.

practice.prompt: We'll go to the beach unless it ___ tomorrow.

explanation.en: Unless means if not, so use a positive present verb.

practice.prompt: Please text me as soon as you ___ at the station.

explanation.en: After as soon as, use the present simple for the future.

practice.prompt: If you heat water to 100 degrees, it ___.

explanation.en: A scientific fact uses the zero conditional: present + present.
